series.name: Flare
historical_notes: One of Cherry Mobile's most popular and longest-running series.
Succeeded by the Aqua series in late 2020.
Included various sub-series like Flare J, Flare S, Flare Y, and Flare X.

series.name: Flare S
historical_notes: A sub-series of the Flare lineup focused on selfie cameras and design.
The Flare S7 and S8 were the last major releases before the transition to Aqua.

series.name: Flare J
historical_notes: Budget-friendly sub-series of the Flare lineup.
Focused on providing essential smartphone features at a low cost.

series.name: Flare Y
characteristics: Android Go edition on some models
historical_notes: Entry-level sub-series of the Flare lineup.
Often featured Android Go edition for optimized performance on low-end hardware.

series.name: Flare X
historical_notes: A short-lived gaming-focused sub-series of the Flare lineup.
Positioned as an 'Ultimate Gaming Experience' device.

series.name: Aqua
historical_notes: Succeeded the Flare series in late 2020.
Represents Cherry Mobile's evolution into the broader CHERRY brand.
Includes gaming-focused models like the Aqua GR.

series.name: Omega
historical_notes: A popular mid-range series in the early 2010s.
Included various models with different screen sizes and processors.

series.name: Desire
historical_notes: A series positioned as elegant and do-it-all smartphones.
Focused on providing a premium look and feel at an affordable price.

series.name: Cosmos
historical_notes: A series that offered premium features like Super AMOLED displays at competitive prices.
The Cosmos One was a limited edition high-end model.

series.name: Cubix
historical_notes: An online-exclusive series sold in partnership with Lazada.
Focused on providing value-for-money smartphones to online consumers.

series.name: Alpha
historical_notes: Cherry Mobile's series of Windows Phone smartphones.
The Alpha Prime 4 and 5 were among the first Windows 10 Mobile phones.

series.name: Rover
target_audience: Budget-conscious users needing a durable phone
characteristics: IP67 or IP68 water and dust resistance
historical_notes: Cherry Mobile's rugged smartphone series.
The Rover 2 was a sequel with IP68 water resistance.

series.name: Defender
target_audience: Power users needing a durable phone
historical_notes: A rugged smartphone with high-end specs for its time.
Designed for active users who need a durable and powerful device.

series.name: Titan
historical_notes: One of Cherry Mobile's early dual-core Android smartphones.
Positioned as a flagship device at the time of its release.

series.name: Thunder
historical_notes: A budget-friendly series that offered good value for money.
The Thunder 2.0 was marketed as one of the cheapest quad-core phones in the Philippines.

series.name: Blaze
historical_notes: A series that offered large-screen smartphones with good specs at competitive prices.
The Blaze 2.0 was a 5.7-inch phablet.

series.name: Sonic
historical_notes: A budget-friendly series that offered good value.
The Sonic 2.0 featured a quad-core processor and Android 4.2 Jelly Bean.

series.name: Burst
historical_notes: An alternative to the Flare series with similar specifications.
Offered good value for budget-conscious consumers.

series.name: Flame
historical_notes: The Flame 2.0 was the first locally branded quad-core smartphone in the Philippines.
Featured a Snapdragon processor.

series.name: ME
historical_notes: A series focused on personalization with customizable back covers.
Allowed users to 'Personalize Me' using an online tool.

series.name: Apollo
historical_notes: A mid-range series that offered good camera features.
The Apollo was a rebranded Cubot GT99.

series.name: Gem
historical_notes: A series of entry-level smartphones named after gemstones.
All models were priced under Php3,000.

series.name: Touch
historical_notes: A budget series that featured On-Cell display technology.
The Touch XL 2 came with a free VR headset.

series.name: Magnum
historical_notes: One of Cherry Mobile's early flagship series.
The Magnum 2X featured a dual-core Nvidia Tegra 2 processor.

series.name: Taiji
characteristics: E-Ink secondary display on the back
historical_notes: An experimental smartphone with a 4.7-inch E-Ink display on the back.
Allowed users to read e-books and view notifications on the E-Ink screen.

series.name: One
historical_notes: Part of Google's Android One initiative.
Offered a stock Android experience with guaranteed updates.

series.name: Superion
historical_notes: Cherry Mobile's series of tablet-phones.
The original Superion was the first tablet phone in the Philippines.

series.name: Rugged R
target_audience: Budget-conscious users needing a durable phone
historical_notes: An affordable rugged smartphone.
Featured a dustproof and waterproof body.

series.name: U Series
historical_notes: A rugged series with a built-in walkie-talkie function.
Designed for camping and outdoor activities.

series.name: Fusion
historical_notes: A series of Android tablets with phone functionality.
Offered large-screen devices at budget-friendly prices.

series.name: Novam
historical_notes: One of Cherry Mobile's early Android smartphones, launched alongside the Magnum HD and Superion.

series.name: Equinox
historical_notes: A smartphone that competed with the Magnum S.

series.name: Life

naming_strategy.description: Cherry Mobile's naming strategy has evolved over time. Early series used simple names like Flare, Omega, and Titan. Within series, they used suffixes like 'HD', 'XL', and numeric iterations (2.0, 3.0) to indicate different models. The Flare series had several sub-series denoted by letters (S, J, Y, X) to indicate different market segments. With the transition to the Aqua series, they adopted a more standardized naming scheme with numbers (S9, S10, S11) and suffixes like Pro, Lite, and Max to denote different tiers within the series.

summary.future_expected_direction: Cherry Mobile is expected to continue focusing on the Aqua series as its main smartphone lineup, with an emphasis on 5G connectivity, gaming performance, and AI-powered camera features. The brand may also explore new form factors like foldables or expand into other IoT devices as part of its evolution into the broader CHERRY brand.
